placements.why: All three segments concern calibration work at an observatory — directives to erase knowledge of it and an assertion it never occurred. No existing strata category holds calibration as an organizational domain.
placements.title: Calibration as an organizational domain
placements.frame: What calibration work does the organization perform, record, or disavow?

placements.title: Commanding the erasure of calibration knowledge from the institutional record
placements.frame: How does the speaker direct the removal of calibration knowledge, and what factual basis is asserted for the erasure?
placements.why: src-1 and src-2 perform imperative directives to forget and remove all knowledge of the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work. src-3 supplies the factual assertion that grounds the erasure — 'The observatory never calibrated it.' Together they name a subject future envelopes could feed: the commanded erasure of calibration records from the institutional memory.
